contentEn:
Replacing a gas furnace with a heat pump in Metro Vancouver is one of the highest-ROI upgrades a homeowner can make in 2026. The equipment costs $12,000–$28,000 installed, but BC Hydro and FortisBC rebates together can cover $5,000–$11,000 of that cost — making the net cost comparable to a new gas furnace with none of the fuel bills. Reno Stars installs heat pumps across Metro Vancouver and manages the rebate paperwork for every project.

Why Metro Vancouver Homeowners Are Switching to Heat Pumps in 2026

Natural gas prices in BC have risen roughly 35% since 2020, and the provincial government has set a hard target of 10% greenhouse gas reduction from buildings by 2030. A new heat pump delivers both space heating and central air conditioning from a single unit, while using roughly half the energy of a gas furnace. For homes with aging furnaces — anything over 15 years old — the math strongly favours replacement before a failure forces an emergency call.

BC's Carbon Tax is scheduled to rise to $170 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent by 2030, which will continue to widen the operating-cost gap between gas and heat pumps. A heat pump installed in 2026 locks in lower operating costs for the 15–20-year lifespan of the equipment.

How Much Does Heat Pump Installation Cost in Vancouver in 2026?

Installed costs for a heat pump replacement in Metro Vancouver typically range from $12,000 to $28,000, depending on home size, existing ductwork, and equipment tier. Here is the cost breakdown homeowners can expect:

  • Entry-level heat pump (single-zone, standard efficiency): $10,000–$15,000 equipment + $2,000–$4,000 installation = $12,000–$19,000 total
  • Mid-range heat pump (multi-zone, high-efficiency): $14,000–$20,000 equipment + $3,000–$5,000 installation = $17,000–$25,000 total
  • Premium cold-climate heat pump (cold-climate rated to −25°C, whole-home): $18,000–$25,000 equipment + $4,000–$6,000 installation = $22,000–$28,000 total

These figures assume a home with existing ductwork. A ductless (mini-split) system typically runs $8,000–$16,000 fully installed. Removing an old gas furnace at the same time adds approximately $500–$1,500 to the job.

BC Hydro and FortisBC Rebates: What Homeowners Can Claim in 2026

Both utilities run rebate programs that can substantially offset the installed cost. Reno Stars helps homeowners identify every applicable rebate and completes the rebate application paperwork as part of the standard project scope.

BC Hydro Rebates

BC Hydro's Better Homes BC program offers up to $5,000 for qualifying heat pump installations. Eligibility requirements include:

  • The heat pump must be listed on BC Hydro's approved products list
  • The system must be installed by a licensed heating contractor
  • Homeowners must apply within 90 days of installation
  • An EnerGuide home assessment before and after installation is required for the top rebate tier

FortisBC Rebates

FortisBC offers an additional rebate of up to $6,000 for heat pump installations in its service territory, which covers most of Metro Vancouver including Vancouver, Burnaby, Coquitlam, Richmond, and Surrey. FortisBC also offers a $300 rebate for the post-installation EnerGuide assessment. When BC Hydro and FortisBC rebates are combined, homeowners can receive $5,000–$11,000 back on a qualifying installation.

Important: FortisBC requires homeowners to submit their application within 90 days of installation. Rebate programs are subject to annual funding caps and can exhaust mid-year — applying early in the calendar year improves the likelihood of receiving the full rebate amount.

What to Expect During the Installation Process

Reno Stars handles the complete heat pump installation from initial assessment through rebate submission. Here is the typical project timeline:

Week 1: Assessment and Quote

A site visit assesses the existing furnace location, ductwork condition, electrical panel capacity, and insulation levels. For most homes in Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, and Coquitlam built after 1980, the existing ductwork is suitable for a standard heat pump with minimal modification. Homes with undersized ducts or older electrical panels may need upgrades before installation — this is identified in writing during the quote.

Week 2–3: Permit Application

Heat pump installations in Metro Vancouver require a building permit. The City of Vancouver, City of Burnaby, City of Coquitlam, and City of Surrey each process heat pump permits within 2–4 weeks. Reno Stars submits the permit application on behalf of the homeowner and coordinates the mandatory electrical inspection.

Week 3–4: Equipment Ordering and Scheduling

Equipment lead times vary by manufacturer and model. Standard-efficiency units are typically available within 1–2 weeks. Cold-climate rated units and premium brands (Mitsubishi, Daikin, Carrier) may require 3–6 weeks. Reno Stars orders equipment after permit approval to avoid holding inventory risk.

Day 1–2: Installation

For a single-family home with existing ductwork, the physical installation typically takes 1–2 days. The old furnace is decommissioned and the outdoor condenser unit is mounted on a pad or wall bracket. The indoor coil is installed in the supply plenum and the refrigerant lines are run. Electrical connections and thermostat wiring complete the mechanical work.

Day 3: Commissioning and Inspection

The system is started, refrigerant charge is verified, airflow is measured, and the thermostat is configured. A city electrical inspector signs off on the work, and the Reno Stars technician walks the homeowner through system operation, maintenance schedule, and filter changes.

Heat Pump vs. Gas Furnace: Operating Cost Comparison in Metro Vancouver

For a typical 2,000 sq ft Vancouver home, here is how annual heating costs compare using Metro Vancouver 2026 utility rates:

SystemAnnual Heating CostAnnual Cooling CostCombined Annual Cost
Gas furnace (92% AFUE)$1,800–$2,400Central AC: $250–$400$2,050–$2,800
Heat pump (HSPF 10+, COP 3.5)$900–$1,400Included$900–$1,400
Annual savings$900–$1,000$250–$400$1,150–$1,400

These figures assume natural gas at approximately $13/GJ and electricity at BC Hydro rates (approximately $0.11/kWh). Heat pump efficiency ratings to look for: HSPF of 10 or above and a COP (Coefficient of Performance) of 3.0 or above at −8°C for Metro Vancouver's winter conditions.

Pairing a Heat Pump with a Critical Load Panel Upgrade

Homes built before 2000 often have 100-amp electrical panels that are not sized for an EV charger, heat pump, and household demand simultaneously. When Reno Stars installs a heat pump, the site assessment checks whether the panel has adequate capacity. If not, a critical load panel upgrade is recommended at the same time — combining the electrical work into a single project reduces labour costs and avoids a second permit and inspection cycle.

Real Project: Heat Pump Pairing in a Vancouver Whole-House Renovation

During a recent whole-house renovation in Vancouver, Reno Stars coordinated a heat pump installation alongside the interior renovation scope. The homeowner upgraded from a 22-year-old gas furnace and a failing window AC unit to a single Mitsubishi cold-climate heat pump, eliminating the window unit and gaining central air conditioning for the first time. The project included a critical load panel assessment and is included in our project portfolio for Vancouver homeowners considering a full-systems upgrade.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does a heat pump last in Metro Vancouver?

A properly installed heat pump in Metro Vancouver typically lasts 15–20 years before the compressor or major components need replacement. Annual maintenance — including filter changes every 1–3 months and a professional service call every 2–3 years — extends the unit's operational lifespan and maintains efficiency.

Do I need a permit to install a heat pump in Vancouver?

Yes. Every city in Metro Vancouver — Vancouver, Burnaby, Coquitlam, Surrey, Richmond, and others — requires a building permit for heat pump installation. An electrical permit is also required for the circuit connecting the outdoor unit. Reno Stars manages both permit applications for homeowners as part of the project scope.

Can a heat pump heat my home in a Vancouver winter?

Modern cold-climate heat pumps are rated to operate efficiently at temperatures as low as −20°C to −25°C, well below any temperature Metro Vancouver experiences. A heat pump with an HSPF rating of 10 or above and a COP of 3.0 or above at −8°C will heat a typical Vancouver home efficiently throughout the winter without supplemental heat in most conditions.

What is the BC government heat pump rebate for 2026?

The combined BC Hydro and FortisBC rebate for qualifying heat pump installations in Metro Vancouver reaches $5,000–$11,000 depending on the utility territory, equipment efficiency tier, and whether an EnerGuide pre- and post-assessment is completed. BC Hydro's program offers up to $5,000 under the Better Homes BC program. FortisBC offers up to $6,000 in its service territory. Rebates are applied retroactively after installation and are paid directly to the homeowner, not deducted from the installation invoice.

Does Reno Stars handle the rebate paperwork?

Yes. Reno Stars completes and submits all required rebate documentation on behalf of homeowners, including the installer declaration form, equipment specifications, and the FortisBC or BC Hydro application. Homeowners are responsible for the optional pre- and post-installation EnerGuide assessment if required for the top rebate tier, which Reno Stars can also coordinate through a certified energy advisor.

contentZh:
2026年，将燃气炉更换为热泵是大温哥华地区业主可做出的最高投资回报项目之一。设备费用为 12,000 至 28,000 加元（含安装），但 BC Hydro 和 FortisBC 的补贴合计可达 5,000 至 11,000 加元，使实际净成本与购买新燃气炉相当，且无需支付燃气账单。Reno Stars 在整个大温哥华地区提供热泵安装服务，并为每个项目办理补贴申请手续。

为什么大温哥华业主在 2026 年转向热泵？

BC 省的天然气价格自 2020 年以来上涨了约 35%，省政府设定的目标是到 2030 年将建筑温室气体排放减少 10%。新型热泵将空间供暖和中央空调合二为一，耗电量约为燃气炉的一半。对于有老旧燃气炉的房屋（使用超过 15 年），在设备故障前主动更换在经济上更为划算。

BC 省的碳税预计将在 2030 年上升至每吨二氧化碳当量 170 加元，这将持续扩大燃气与热泵之间的运营成本差距。2026 年安装的热泵可锁定未来 15–20 年设备寿命期内的更低运营成本。

2026 年温哥华热泵安装费用是多少？

大温哥华地区热泵更换的安装费用通常在 12,000 至 28,000 加元之间，具体取决于房屋面积、现有管道系统和设备等级。以下是业主可以参考的费用明细：

  • 入门级热泵（单区域、标准能效）：设备 10,000–15,000 加元 + 安装 2,000–4,000 加元 = 总计 12,000–19,000 加元
  • 中档热泵（多区域、高能效）：设备 14,000–20,000 加元 + 安装 3,000–5,000 加元 = 总计 17,000–25,000 加元
  • 顶级低温气候型热泵（耐低温至零下 25°C，全屋型）：设备 18,000–25,000 加元 + 安装 4,000–6,000 加元 = 总计 22,000–28,000 加元

以上为现有管道系统住宅的估算。无管道（分体式）系统通常全包装费用为 8,000–16,000 加元。同时拆除旧燃气炉另加约 500–1,500 加元。

BC Hydro 和 FortisBC 补贴：2026 年业主可申请多少？

两家公用事业公司均提供可大幅抵消安装成本的补贴计划。Reno Stars 帮助业主识别每项适用的补贴，并作为标准项目范围的一部分完成补贴申请文件的填写。

BC Hydro 补贴

BC Hydro 的 Better Homes BC 计划为符合条件的热泵安装提供最高 5,000 加元的补贴。资格要求包括：

  • 热泵必须在 BC Hydro 批准产品清单上
  • 系统必须由持牌供暖承包商安装
  • 业主必须在安装后 90 天内提交申请
  • 最高补贴等级需要安装前后的 EnerGuide 房屋评估

FortisBC 补贴

FortisBC 在其服务区域内为热泵安装提供额外的最高 6,000 加元补贴，服务区域覆盖大温哥华大部分地区，包括温哥华、本拿比、高贵林、列治文和素里。FortisBC 还为安装后的 EnerGuide 评估提供 300 加元补贴。BC Hydro 和 FortisBC 补贴合计，业主可获得 5,000 至 11,000 加元的返还。

重要提示：FortisBC 要求业主在安装后 90 天内提交申请。补贴计划受年度资金上限约束，可能在年中耗尽——在年初尽早申请可提高获得全额补贴的可能性。

安装流程：各阶段详情

Reno Stars 从初步评估到补贴提交，全程处理热泵安装的完整流程。典型项目时间线如下：

第 1 周：评估和报价

现场踏勘评估现有炉具位置、管道状况、电箱容量和保温水平。对于 1980 年后建造的大多数温哥华、本拿比、列治文和高贵林住宅，现有管道系统适用于标准热泵，无需大幅改造。管道尺寸不足或电箱老旧的住宅，可能需要在安装前进行升级——这在报价阶段以书面形式说明。

第 2–3 周：许可证申请

大温哥华地区热泵安装需要建筑许可证。温哥华市、本拿比市、高贵林市和素里市各自在 2–4 周内处理热泵许可证。Reno Stars 代表业主提交许可证申请，并协调强制性电气检查。

第 3–4 周：设备订购和排期

设备交货时间因制造商和型号而异。标准能效机组通常在 1–2 周内有货。耐低温机组和高端品牌（三菱、大金、开利）可能需要 3–6 周。Reno Stars 在许可证批准后订购设备，以避免库存风险。

安装第 1–2 天：安装施工

对于配有现有管道系统的独立住宅，物理安装通常需要 1–2 天。旧炉具被停用，室外冷凝机组安装在底座或壁挂支架上。室内盘管安装在供气管道中，制冷剂管道铺设到位，电气连接和恒温器线路完成机械工作。

安装第 3 天：调试和验收

系统启动，制冷剂充注量验证，风量测量，恒温器配置完成。市政电气检查员签署验收文件，Reno Stars 技术人员向业主讲解系统操作，维护计划和滤网更换周期。

热泵与燃气炉：运营成本对比

以典型 2,000 平方英尺温哥华住宅为例，使用 2026 年大温哥华地区费率，各供暖系统年度费用对比如下：

系统年度供暖费用年度制冷费用合计年度费用
燃气炉（92% 能效）1,800–2,400 加元中央空调：250–400 加元2,050–2,800 加元
热泵（HSPF 10+，能效比 3.5）900–1,400 加元含在内900–1,400 加元
年度节省900–1,000 加元250–400 加元1,150–1,400 加元

以上按天然气约 13 加元/千兆焦耳和 BC Hydro 电价约 0.11 加元/千瓦时计算。选购热泵时应关注能效指标：HSPF 10 及以上，−8°C 时能效比（COP）3.0 及以上，可适应大温哥华的冬季条件。

同时升级热泵与关键负载电箱

2000 年前建造的住宅通常配有 100 安培电箱，无法同时容纳电动汽车充电器、热泵和日常家庭用电。Reno Stars 安装热泵时，现场评估会检查电箱是否有足够容量。如果没有，建议同时进行关键负载电箱升级——将电气工程合并为一个项目可降低人工成本，避免第二次许可证和检查周期。关键负载电箱升级服务请浏览关键负载电箱安装页面。

真实项目：温哥华全屋装修中的热泵配套安装

在最近进行的温哥华全屋装修项目中，Reno Stars 将热泵安装与室内装修范围同步协调。业主将使用了 22 年的旧燃气炉和一台故障窗式空调更换为单一三菱耐低温热泵，消除了窗式空调，并首次获得中央空调。该项目包含关键负载电箱评估，已收入我们的项目作品集，供考虑全屋系统升级的温哥华业主参考。具体项目详情请查看：温哥华全屋定制装修项目。

规划厨房、浴室、全屋或商业装修？立即联系 Reno Stars 获取免费、无义务报价。

常见问题

热泵在大温哥华能用多少年？

正确安装的大温哥华热泵通常在使用 15–20 年后才需要更换压缩机或主要部件。每年维护（包括每 1–3 个月更换滤网和每 2–3 年进行一次专业维护）可延长机组使用寿命并保持能效。

在温哥华安装热泵需要许可证吗？

需要。大温哥华每个城市——温哥华、本拿比、高贵林、素里、列治文等——都要求热泵安装持有建筑许可证。室外机组电路连接还需要电气许可证。Reno Stars 代表业主管理两项许可证申请，作为项目范围的一部分。

热泵能在温哥华的冬天为我的房屋供暖吗？

现代耐低温热泵的运行效率可达零下 20°C 至零下 25°C，远低于大温哥华任何冬季温度。HSPF 10 及以上、−8°C 时 COP 3.0 及以上的热泵，在大多数条件下能高效为典型温哥华住宅供暖，无需补充供暖。

2026 年 BC 省热泵补贴是多少？

大温哥华地区符合条件热泵安装的 BC Hydro 和 FortisBC 合计补贴可达 5,000 至 11,000 加元，具体金额取决于公用事业服务区域、设备能效等级以及是否完成安装前后的 EnerGuide 评估。BC Hydro 的 Better Homes BC 计划提供最高 5,000 加元。FortisBC 在其服务区域提供最高 6,000 加元。补贴在安装后追溯支付，直接支付给业主，不从安装发票中扣除。

Reno Stars 是否协助办理补贴手续？

是的。Reno Stars 代表业主填写并提交所有必需的补贴文件，包括安装商声明表、设备规格以及 FortisBC 或 BC Hydro 的申请表。业主负责最高补贴等级所需的可选安装前后 EnerGuide 评估，Reno Stars 也可通过认证能源顾问协调安排。

规划厨房、浴室、全屋或商业装修？立即联系 Reno Stars 获取免费、无义务报价。
